facts.raw_span: A 4-year-old girl was brought for evaluation of a slowly enlarging mass on the dorsal aspect of her right wrist, first noted 2 months earlier
The lesion caused pain and discomfort but no functional limitation
There was no history of trauma, other lesions, or relevant family or medical history
a 1.5 × 1.5 cm firm, tender mass with intact overlying skin was located medial to Lister’s tubercle
wrist range of motion was normal, sensation was intact, and pulses were palpable
The mass moved with extension of the right index finger

Ultrasound showed a well-defined, multilobulated, mildly echogenic swelling measuring 1.5 × 1.0 × 0.5 cm with some vascularity, lying within the fourth extensor tendon compartment adjacent to the extensor indicis proprius tendon
the working diagnosis was a giant‐cell tumor of the tendon sheath
No further imaging was performed
